stories.headline: 24 whales die in stranding
stories.summary: Twenty-four sperm whales have died after stranding on Ninety Mile Beach in New Zealand's far north, with burials under way on Friday.

stories.headline: Tonga declares emergency
stories.summary: Tonga's government has declared a 27-day state of emergency as the El Niño drought gripping much of the Pacific worsens, RNZ Pacific reported.

stories.headline: Worst week since 2020
stories.summary: Asian markets closed Friday with their worst week since 2020: the Nikkei fell 5%, the KOSPI 5.2% and Taiwan 6.2%, as the AI sell-off deepened after Anthropic's debut.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall
stories.summary: Severe Cyclone Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur on Friday morning with winds gusting to 90 km/h, after more than 300,000 people were evacuated.

stories.headline: Pakistan seal Test series 1-0
stories.summary: Pakistan chased down 90 in 13 overs on day four in Rawalpindi on Friday to beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets and complete a 1-0 series victory, their first in two years.

stories.headline: Saudi stops Houthi missile
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia said its air defences destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile over its southern region on Friday and intercepted drones near Jazan, Abha and Khamis Mushait.

stories.headline: COP31 slips into overtime
stories.summary: The COP31 climate talks in Antalya slipped into overtime on Friday, with nearly 200 countries still split over fossil fuels and climate finance and no deal agreed.

stories.headline: Mass missile attack on Kyiv
stories.summary: Russia launched Tu-160 bombers, ballistic missiles and drones at Ukraine overnight, setting fires across Kyiv days after Putin vowed retaliation for a Crimean Bridge strike.

stories.headline: 581 women killed Jul-Sep
stories.summary: South Africa's latest quarterly crime statistics, released Friday, recorded 581 women killed between July and September, among 5,590 murders nationwide in the quarter.

stories.headline: Angola buys into De Beers
stories.summary: Angola will pay about $180 million for a 10% stake in diamond giant De Beers, state miner Endiama's chief executive said on Friday, as Luanda also opened its first gold refinery.

stories.headline: Alcaraz sweeps ATP group
stories.summary: Carlos Alcaraz eased hamstring fears by beating Flavio Cobolli 6-4 6-1 in Turin on Friday, completing a perfect ATP Finals group stage ahead of a semi-final with Ben Shelton.

stories.headline: UK-EU trade deal sealed
stories.summary: Britain and the EU agreed deals at Friday's Brussels summit to ease food trade, let 100,000 young people a year work across the Channel, and link emissions trading from 2028.

stories.headline: Cancer pill stuns trial
stories.summary: A pill, daraxonrasib, combined with chemotherapy stopped pancreatic tumours growing in 90% of trial patients and made them vanish completely in one in 12.

stories.headline: Anthropic closes up 17%
stories.summary: Anthropic shares closed their first day at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price, valuing the AI company at about $1.3 trillion after the biggest debut on record.

stories.headline: GTA VI day one tops $2.3bn
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI sold an estimated 24.58 million copies in its first day for about $2.36 billion, nearly triple GTA V's debut, according to Sensor Tower estimates.

stories.headline: Dollar hits 19-month high
stories.summary: The dollar rose to a 19-month high on Friday, its fourth straight weekly gain, as the yen slid to 159.50 and gold headed for a 7.3% weekly loss.

stories.text: Man charged with terrorism offences after a raid
stories.summary: An Australian man was charged with terrorism-related offences on Friday after police raided his Sydney home; two other men face hindering and firearms charges.

stories.text: Ex-opposition leader Speakman quits politics
stories.summary: Mark Speakman, the former New South Wales opposition leader, announced on Friday he is quitting politics, the eighth Liberal MP to depart as the party trails in polls.

stories.text: US sanctions Comanchero figures, an Australian first
stories.summary: US sanctions targeting figures linked to the Comanchero motorcycle club, including two founding members living in New Zealand, were welcomed by NZ Police on Friday.

stories.text: AFL draft completes Friday night, 65 picks
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL national draft wrapped up on Friday night in Melbourne, with rounds two to six completing the 65-pick draft after Thursday's first round of 19 selections.

stories.text: Core inflation 2.2% in Oct, above BoJ target
stories.summary: Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October, above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for a second straight month, fuelling expectations of a December rate hike.

stories.text: Storm leaves 20,000 without power
stories.summary: Storms brought down transmission towers on South Australia's Eyre Peninsula, cutting power to 20,000 people and closing schools, with repairs still under way Friday.

stories.text: Court upholds Kakao founder Kim's acquittal
stories.summary: A Seoul appeals court on Friday upheld the acquittal of Kakao founder Kim Beom-su on charges of manipulating SM Entertainment's share price, rejecting prosecutors' appeal.

stories.text: 98 caught cheating in entrance exam
stories.summary: South Korea's Education Ministry said 98 people were caught cheating in this year's College Scholastic Ability Test, including five who used smart devices.

stories.text: Samsung names new chip and mobile chiefs
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics kept its dual leadership under Jeon Young-hyun and Roh Tae-moon in a Friday reshuffle, naming new heads for its memory chip and mobile businesses.

stories.text: Presidency neutral on impeachment push
stories.summary: South Korea's presidential office said Friday it has no position on the ruling Democratic Party's push to impeach Chief Justice Jo Hee-de after a Supreme Court remand.

stories.text: Four weather systems drench the Philippines
stories.summary: PAGASA warned Friday that four weather systems at once would bring heavy rain to the Philippines, with 50-100 mm expected in Cagayan and Isabela provinces.

stories.text: Lending rates held 18th month: 1-yr 3.00%
stories.summary: China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for an 18th straight month on Friday, holding the one-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and the five-year at 3.50%.

stories.text: Brent up 0.3% to $92.22 on tanker reports
stories.summary: Brent crude rose 24 cents to $92.22 early Friday on Houthi attacks on Riyadh and reported tanker disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, though it still faces a weekly fall.

stories.text: Australia U-17s stun Argentina 2-0 at World Cup
stories.summary: Australia's Joeys opened their Under-17 World Cup campaign in Qatar with a shock 2-0 win over Argentina, inspired by Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon.

stories.text: Fuel crisis: overnight queues, 20L ration
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported Friday from Blantyre that Malawi's fuel crisis has motorists queuing for hours or all night, with purchases rationed to 20 litres and a black market booming.

stories.text: Rand at 1-year low, 17.56 per dollar
stories.summary: The South African rand touched a one-year low early Friday, at 17.56 to the dollar, as coalition talks after local elections and a stronger dollar weighed on the currency.

stories.text: Nigeria urges more farm, small-business finance
stories.summary: Nigeria's government on Friday urged lenders to expand affordable finance for agriculture and small businesses, with Vice President Shettima speaking in Abuja.

stories.text: Davis Cup captain Smith to step down
stories.summary: Leon Smith, Britain's longest-serving Davis Cup captain, will step down after next week's Finals in Bologna, the LTA confirmed on Friday, ending almost 17 years in charge.

stories.text: Lagarde's final speech warns on AI cyber risk
stories.summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde, in her eighth and final Frankfurt Banking Congress speech, urged Europe to act early and called AI-boosted cyber threats her top worry.

stories.text: Young Europeans rally in 7 countries on costs
stories.summary: Unions and youth groups held coordinated Friday rallies in seven European countries over housing costs, stagnant pay and military spending, with a general strike in Italy.

stories.text: Fridges secured from hackers in secret op
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of internet-connected fridges across the UK have been secured against hackers in a secret nationwide operation, the BBC reported.

stories.text: Retail sales +0.7%; borrowing under forecast
stories.summary: UK retail sales volumes unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October, while government borrowing came in at £17 billion, below the £18 billion forecast, the ONS said Friday.

stories.text: Anthropic -7.6% to $89.75 early Fri, day two
stories.summary: Anthropic shares fell 7.6% to $89.75 in early Friday trading, sliding toward their $83 IPO price a day after closing up 17% on a record-breaking debut.

stories.text: Netflix, Amazon, Fox bid for 2030 Cup rights
stories.summary: Netflix, Amazon, YouTube and Fox have bid for US rights to the 2030 World Cup, estimated at more than $1.5 billion, while Disney's ESPN sat out, Yonhap reported.

stories.text: Texans rout Colts 26-3, Stroud throws 3 TDs
stories.summary: The Houston Texans beat the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 in Thursday night football, with C.J. Stroud throwing three touchdown passes for 194 yards.

stories.text: Rain wipes out GP practice, no timed lap
stories.summary: Heavy rain left standing water on the Las Vegas street circuit, so no driver set a timed lap in Thursday's opening practice; dry weather is forecast for Friday qualifying.

stories.text: Michigan sentiment final 51.5, up from 48.0
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's final November consumer sentiment reading came in at 51.5 on Friday, up from October's 48.0, with one-year inflation expectations cut to 3.7%.
stories.source: University of Michigan via Exchange Rates UK
